subject: Action items and artifacts: CareHorizon pilot eval schema & prompt bank
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Emma Brooks <emma.brooks@carehorizon.com>, CareHorizon Procurement <procurement@carehorizon.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: pilot eval artifacts, next steps and data spec

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we all have the same checklist for the pilot eval on Redwood: 

Recap (short):
- Goal: run a 2-week, customer-specific evaluation to validate model fit for CH’s triage / routing prompts, measure answer quality and regression risk versus your current endpoint.
- Scope: ~2k labelled samples for scoring; a small live-sample holdout for gating; prompts + expected outputs in JSONL.
- Success metrics: >=92% high-confidence routing accuracy (primary), semantic similarity >=0.85 on open-answer checks, no more than 2% critical hallucinations in the scored set.

Next steps (action owners & timing):
1) We’ll send a recommended prompt bank and schema (Jordan) — attached: carehorizon_prompt_bank_v1.jsonl. Target: today EOD.
2) Redwood will share the eval schema and scorer rubric (Ben) — attached: redwood_eval_schema_v2.md. Target: 9/16.
3) CareHorizon to confirm dataset export format and provide sample of 200 rows for ingestion test (Emma/Procurement). Target: 9/18.
4) Contract/SLA draft for the pilot (Jordan + Procurement) — attached draft: SLA-draft-CH-2026.pdf. Please flag any procurement redlines.

Technical notes / recommendations (Ben included on this thread):
- Recommended model starting point: Redwood-verified medium family (13B quantized variant) for parity with your latency targets; we also suggest a smaller 7B instruct model for fast A/B throughput checks during the first 48 hours.
- Scoring approach: JSONL with fields {id, prompt, expected, label, metadata}; use exact-match for structured routing labels and contrastive-similarity for free-text clarification answers.
- We’ll provide a scoring harness and continuous-regression alert hooks in the dashboard.

Emma — could you confirm: any internal PII redaction steps we need to apply before you share the 200-row sample? If yes, we can run an ingestion test on a redacted dataset.

Attachments: carehorizon_prompt_bank_v1.jsonl (prompt examples), redwood_eval_schema_v2.md (scoring rubric), SLA-draft-CH-2026.pdf (pilot terms).

Thanks — Jordan
--
Jordan Blake
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0124
From: Emma Brooks <emma.brooks@carehorizon.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: CareHorizon Procurement <procurement@carehorizon.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: pilot eval artifacts, next steps and data spec

Thanks Jordan — this is exactly the level of detail we needed. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PII: We can export a de-identified sample by EOD Friday (9/18). We will remove MRNs and replace patient names with pseudonyms; timestamps remain.
- Sample: I’ll drop a 200-row CSV into the Drive link you sent. Will the ingestion test accept CSV or must it be JSONL?
- SLA: Procurement flagged a 30-day data retention limit for the pilot analytics — can Redwood confirm that’s doable?

Two questions about the scoring rubric: 
1) For the semantic similarity threshold (0.85) — is that cosine on embedding space? Which embedding model will Redwood use for scoring?
2) For the hallucination checks, can we define examples of what you’d consider critical vs. non-critical hallucinations? We want to align expectations before scoring.

I’ll upload the sample and a short readme about our label taxonomy tomorrow.

—Emma
Emma Brooks
Head of Care Insights | CareHorizon Health
emma.brooks@carehorizon.com | +1 (617) 555-0199
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Emma Brooks <emma.brooks@carehorizon.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Sep 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: pilot eval artifacts, next steps and data spec

Hi Emma — quick answers and concrete guidance so your team can prepare the sample with minimal friction.

1) Ingestion formats: We accept JSONL (preferred) and CSV. For CSV, please include a header row and map columns to the schema fields in redwood_eval_schema_v2.md. We’ll do the conversion on intake if needed.

2) Embedding & similarity: Yes — semantic similarity in the rubric is cosine over Redwood’s embed-compat vector (embedding model: redwood-embed-2-small). We’ll surface both the similarity score and an excerpted rationale for anything that falls below threshold.

3) Hallucination taxonomy (draft):
- Critical hallucination: output asserts factually verifiable medical advice or patient data that would materially change triage outcome (e.g., incorrectly stating a diagnosis or prescribing a medication).
- Non-critical hallucination: minor factual drift, formatting mismatches, or missing source citations where not required.
We’ll include 6 example cases in the scoring rubric (see redwood_eval_schema_v2.md). Please flag any of those examples that you disagree with and we’ll adjust.

4) Models & gating strategy: for the pilot we recommend the following plan —
  a) Start: L7-instruct-7B (fast) for warmup + latency baseline.
  b) Primary candidate: R-13B-quant (balanced latency and quality).
  c) Fallback: R-7B-quant as cost-optimized option for scale testing.
We’ll run the scoring against both primary and fallback to measure regression risk.

5) Data retention / SLA note: 30-day retention for pilot logs and scored artifacts is acceptable. For any longer-term storage we’ll capture your consent in the follow-on contract.

6) Ingestion test: please upload a 200-row sample to the Drive link (I’ll watch for it) and CC procurement so we can provision the limited pilot workspace. We’ll ingest redacted rows and run a conversion demo within 24 hours.

If you’re comfortable, Jordan and I can schedule a 30-minute intake tomorrow to walk through the sample mapping.

Best — Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Post-call: pilot eval artifacts, next steps and data spec

Thanks Ben — that all sounds good. We uploaded a 200-row sample (CSV) to the Drive folder and added a short README mapping our columns to the taxonomy. I’ve redacted PII as discussed. 

Procurement is reviewing the SLA draft and will send redlines by Monday. We’re happy to do the 30-min intake on Monday afternoon — either 1:00pm or 3:00pm PT works for our team.

One more ask: could Redwood provide a short list of the exact inference latency SLOs you expect for R-13B-quant at 8-token median and at 64-token median? Procurement is focused on performance guarantees for patient-facing flows.

Emma
